title: Infrastructure Is Becoming Ineffective
text:
Infrastructure Is Becoming Ineffective

Wei He

Gavekal Dragonomics | 29 Sep 2026

As China’s economic growth has faltered this year, the government has promised to do more to bolster demand, particularly investment. Yet the usually reliable counter-cyclical support from infrastructure spending has not been forthcoming: year-to-date through August, fixed-asset investment in infrastructure sectors is down 5.4%. More policy support and new projects are still being rolled out, so it is possible, even likely, that the infrastructure numbers will get a bit better in the remaining months of 2026. But even so, it will be hard for infrastructure investment to play a major role in stabilizing growth this year.This weak performance from infrastructure is more than just a misfire on the timing of policy and project approvals. It reflects the cumulative impact of a more cautious approach to funding and approving local infrastructure projects that has been developing for almost a decade. Stricter financial supervision has depleted the pipeline of planned infrastructure projects that can be quickly started. And local officials currently have particularly strong incentives not to take risks with debt-funded projects, as the anti-corruption campaign is ramping up and political scrutiny is intensifying ahead of the personnel turnover at the 2027 Party Congress (see Governance Over Growth).
